acceptance: The probe reports every carried patch that conflicts or is empty on the probed upstream commit, not only the first; patches after a failing one are still tested.

A patch whose result may depend on an earlier failed patch is identified as such in its issue (for example by naming the earlier failed patches it was replayed without), so knock-on conflicts are not mistaken for independent drift.
The controller keeps one open drift issue per failing patch and closes a patch's issue only when that patch applies on the probed commit.
A controller test with two drifting patches, where only the earlier one is later fixed, keeps the later patch's issue open; a test where a later patch's paths change updates only that issue.
The first-red rule still holds: a run fails when it opens a drift issue or changes an issue's key, and stays green when every drift issue is unchanged.
The run summary lists every failing patch with its kind and paths.

After the fix is merged, a dry-run dispatch of benchbox-upstream.yml lists every patch that fails on current upstream main, and issue #91 is reopened or replaced if spark-databricks-regexp-trunc still fails.
context:
Decision gate: a patch that applies only on top of an earlier patch that failed cannot be tested in isolation. Choose and record one rule before coding: (a) skip the failed patch and keep replaying, reporting later failures that may be knock-on effects; or (b) report later patches as untested. Default to (a) with the issue body saying the result assumes earlier failed patches were skipped, unless an owner prefers (b). No other owner decision is needed; the issue-per-patch and first-red rules were already approved on 2026-11-14.

Verification rubric: (1) new probe and controller tests fail on main 19ddf096 and pass after the fix; (2) python -m unittest tests.test_downstream_controller tests.test_downstream_refresh tests.test_downstream_contract passes; (3) live dry run shows all failing patches on upstream main and changes no repository state; (4) the next scheduled run leaves one open issue per failing patch.

Guardrails: refresh auto, candidate and integrate keep stopping at the first conflict, because a refresh must not publish a partial replay; this change is to the probe report only. The prepare job stays read-only and the publish job stays the only issue writer (test_write_capability_is_confined_to_the_controller_publisher must pass unchanged). Do not change the drift marker format in a way that orphans open issues; existing issues must be matched or closed by the new code. Do not add per-patch API calls beyond one upsert or close per changed issue.

Review 2026-11-17 (todo review, L2): added acceptance for knock-on conflicts and for the run summary. A probe exception (status failed, for example an original file now upstream) still yields a single probe-failed note with no issue; that behaviour is kept. Notification of these issues is tracked separately in controller-issues-have-no-owner-or-notification-20261117. A local probe call with a relative root (Path('.')) misreports a missing patch file; production passes an absolute ROOT, so it is not in scope.

Owner decision 2026-11-17 (choice dialog): option (a). Keep replaying past a failed patch and open one issue per failing patch; each issue names the earlier failed patches it was replayed without. Lands in one fork PR with controller-issues-have-no-owner-or-notification-20261117 and fork-workflow-actions-run-on-deprecated-node20-20261117; the owner reviews that PR because it changes workflows.
description: downstream.refresh.probe replays carried patches in manifest order and stops at the first RefreshConflict, so a controller run sees at most one drifting patch. Controller.drift then closes every other entry's drift issue before upserting the new one. On 2026-11-16 (run 43881204346) postgres-exact-division (manifest index 29) began to conflict on upstream main e31d209e, and the run closed issue #91 for spark-databricks-regexp-trunc (index 51) although that patch still conflicts. A replay of every carried patch on upstream v30.33.0 that continues past failures finds five conflicts: postgres-exact-division (sqlglot/generators/postgres.py), spark-databricks-regexp-trunc (tests/dialects/test_exasol.py, tests/dialects/test_oracle.py), sqlite-empty-group-by, sqlite-index-null-ordering and sqlite-pivot-lowering (all sqlglot/generators/sqlite.py). Only one is visible on the fork's issue list. A closed drift issue therefore does not mean the patch applies again, and maintainers learn about broken patches one per day.
